name: Radium-223 dichloride (bone-metastatic mCRPC, no visceral metastases)
stage: M1 CRPC (metastatic castration-resistant, symptomatic bone metastases, no visceral metastases)

biomarkers.note: Radium-223 is an alpha-emitting bone-targeting radiopharmaceutical for symptomatic bone-metastatic disease; it is not molecularly biomarker-gated. It has not been shown to extend survival in patients with visceral metastases or bulky (>3 to 4 cm) nodal disease and must not be used with visceral metastases. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Prostate Cancer, PROS-J (Radiopharmaceutical Therapy) and DeVita 12th ed. (ALSYMPCA).

lineOfTherapy: category 1 option for symptomatic bone metastases in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer without visceral metastases; may be combined with enzalutamide and a bone-health agent

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: castration-resistant prostate cancer with symptomatic bone metastases and no visceral metastases
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v6.2026, PROS-J (Radiopharmaceutical Therapy, Radium-223), prostate lines 3828 to 3830

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: ongoing ADT to maintain castrate testosterone below 50 ng/dL

exclusionCriteria.locator: v6.2026, PROS-18 footnote ooo, prostate line 1829 (Radium-223 should not be used in patients with visceral metastases); PROS-J, prostate line 3830

drugs.name: Radium-223 dichloride

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
provenance.locator: line 162484 (ALSYMPCA: six injections of radium-223 at a dose of 50 kBq per kilogram of body weight intravenously, one injection administered every 4 weeks)

drugs.notes: SOURCE-STATED DOSE: 50 kBq/kg IV once every 4 weeks for 6 injections (ALSYMPCA phase III; DeVita 12th ed. line 162484). The numeric value 50 is source-established and recorded in dosePerUnit. HOWEVER basis and unit are set to the literal VERIFY because the current standard-protocol schema cannot represent this dose: the basis enum [bsa, mgkg, flat, auc] has no kilobecquerel-per-kilogram-body-weight (kBq/kg) radioactivity basis, and the unit enum [mg/m2, mg/kg, mg, AUC, units, mCi, GBq] has no kBq/kg token. These two fields are VERIFY pending a schema extension for radioactivity-per-body-weight units, NOT because the dose is unknown. Note: the current product label activity is commonly cited as 55 kBq/kg after a 2015 recalibration, but that value is not in the provided sources, so it was not used (no invention). The SCHEDULE (every 4 weeks, 6 injections) is fully source-grounded and encoded in days/cycleLengthDays/cycles. Radioligand: no ISMP tall-man form.

supportiveCare: continue ADT to maintain castrate testosterone below 50 ng/dL (PROS-G).

bone-health agent: concomitant denosumab or zoledronic acid is recommended, because radium-223 may increase fracture risk when given with an ARPI without a bone-health agent (PROS-J, prostate line 3836).

concurrent enzalutamide plus a bone-health agent may be considered given the overall-survival benefit over enzalutamide alone (PROS-J, prostate line 3833); combination with abiraterone increased fractures (avoid).
no concurrent cytotoxic chemotherapy: combining radium-223 with chemotherapy (e.g. docetaxel) is not established and increases myelosuppression; sequence rather than combine, per radium-223 labeling.
administer by an appropriately licensed nuclear-medicine/radiation-oncology facility with radiation-safety precautions.

monitoring: CBC before treatment initiation and before each subsequent dose (myelosuppression; PROS-J, prostate line 7916)
PSA and serum testosterone (confirm castrate level)
fracture risk / bone health, especially if combined with an ARPI

doseModificationRules.condition: hematologic toxicity (inadequate counts before a dose)
doseModificationRules.text: Hold or discontinue radium-223 per labeling and radiation-safety protocol for inadequate marrow recovery; obtain clinical review.

core.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
core.locator: line 162484 (ALSYMPCA: 922 patients; six injections of radium-223 at 50 kBq/kg IV every 4 weeks; improved median overall survival 14 vs 11.2 months)

guideline.locator: PROS-J (Radiopharmaceutical Therapy, Radium-223): administered IV once a month for 6 months (prostate line 3832); symptomatic bone metastases without visceral disease (prostate lines 3828 to 3830); bone-health agent recommendation (prostate line 3836); PROS-18 footnote ooo (no visceral metastases), prostate line 1829; Discussion CBC before each dose (prostate line 7916). Activity dose (kBq/kg) is not stated on PROS-J.

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for radium-223 dichloride in symptomatic bone-metastatic mCRPC without visceral metastases (disease #54 mCRPC). The source-stated activity dose is 50 kBq/kg IV every 4 weeks for 6 injections (ALSYMPCA phase III; DeVita 12th ed. line 162484); the schedule (cycleLengthDays 28, cycles 6) is fully grounded to DeVita line 162484 and Standard Guidelines (NCCN) Prostate v6.2026 PROS-J (prostate line 3832, once a month for 6 months). The numeric activity value 50 is recorded in dosePerUnit, but drug basis and unit are set to VERIFY because the current schema enums cannot represent a kilobecquerel-per-kilogram-body-weight (kBq/kg) radioactivity dose (basis enum lacks a per-body-weight radioactivity basis; unit enum has only mCi/GBq, not kBq/kg). These two VERIFY fields reflect a schema representation gap, not missing evidence, and are listed in verifyFields (status remains DRAFT). The commonly cited 55 kBq/kg label activity (post-2015 recalibration) is not in the provided sources and was deliberately not substituted (no invention). Visceral metastases are an exclusion (PROS-J, PROS-18 footnote ooo). A concomitant bone-health agent is recommended. No dose was invented or inferred. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
